desc:
A Framer site audit and design review gives you a plain, ranked list of what to fix on your site and why. Ecom Swift LLC checks your Framer project as a visitor and as a builder, then hands you a written report you can act on yourself or hand to us.

## What is a Framer site audit?

A Framer site audit is a structured review of a live Framer project that finds problems in design, mobile layout, speed, search setup, forms, links and project organization. The output is a report, not a rebuild. Each finding says what is wrong, how serious it is, why it matters and how to fix it.

We never change your site during the audit. You keep full control and decide which fixes to make, in which order, and who does them.

## Why a Framer site drifts out of shape

Framer makes it easy to publish quickly, and that speed is the reason sites collect small problems. A section gets copied and edited on desktop but never checked on a phone. A page is duplicated and keeps the old title. An image is dropped in at full size. A form stops sending to the right inbox after a change and nobody notices for weeks.

None of these problems shows up in the editor canvas. They show up when a real visitor on a real phone tries to read a page, tap a button or send a message. An audit finds them before a visitor or a client does.

## How an audit improves results

Most Framer sites exist to produce something: enquiries, bookings, sign-ups or trust in a brand. Each problem on the site removes a little of that. A heading that is hard to read on a small screen loses a reader. A button that links to a deleted page loses a lead. A slow hero image loses patience.

A ranked list matters because your time is limited. Fixing a broken contact form is worth more than adjusting spacing in the footer. The report puts the changes that protect leads and visibility first, so the first hour of work goes where it helps most.

## What a thorough Framer audit covers

- Layout at phone, tablet and desktop breakpoints, including text wrapping, tap targets and overlapping elements.
- Page speed, with attention to hero images, video, fonts and heavy effects.
- Image sizes, formats and file names.
- Every link, button and form, tested with a real submission.
- Page titles, descriptions and heading order on the pages that matter most.
- Project structure: page naming, reused components, styles and unused leftovers.
- The wording of headlines and buttons, and whether the page says its point early.
- Tracking tools and cookie notices, and whether they match what the site actually does.
- Consistency of colors, type sizes and spacing across pages.
- A priority order for every finding, from fix this week to fix later.

## How the work runs

We open your live site first and use it the way a first-time visitor would, on a phone and on a laptop. Then we look at the project itself, with view access, to see how it is built and where it could break.

Findings go into one PDF report, ranked by importance. The Basic package covers design, mobile layout, speed, links and forms. Standard adds search and project structure, plus a video call where we explain the top fixes and answer questions. Premium goes further with a look at page messages and buttons, tracking and privacy, a three-month fix roadmap, a re-check of the top fixes after you have made them, and a longer call.

If you want us to make the fixes, we can quote them as a separate job. The report is useful whether or not you hire us for that.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Tell us the main goal of the site, so we can rank findings against it.
- Share the pages you worry about most.
- Mention anything you changed recently.
- Read the top of the report first and start with the highest-ranked items.
- Re-test the site on your own phone after each fix.

**Avoid:**
- Editing the site while we review it, because the findings may no longer match.
- Treating every finding as equally urgent.
- Fixing cosmetic items before broken forms and links.
- Skipping the mobile review because the desktop version looks fine.
- Waiting until a redesign to deal with small, cheap problems.

## Who this is for

An audit suits a founder whose site was built quickly and who wants to know if it is ready for visitors. It suits a freelancer or small team that inherited a Framer project and does not know what is fragile in it. It also suits a business owner about to spend on ads or a launch who wants the site checked first.

Small sites benefit too. A short site with a broken form or a missing mobile layout loses just as much as a large one.

## What we need from you

Send the live site address and a line or two about what the site should achieve. For the project review, invite us as a viewer or collaborator in Framer, so we can see the structure without needing your password. We never ask for passwords.

If you want a call, tell us your time zone and a few windows that work. After you order, we send a short checklist and keep you updated until the report is delivered.
